(PER: HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE K S HEMALEKHA) Assailing the correctness and legality of the judgment and award dated 13.05.2024 in M.V.C.No.494/2022 on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T, Kalaburagi (hereinafter referred to as "Tribunal" for short) the Insurance Company has preferred the present appeal.

2. In a road traffic accident that occurred on 14.12.2021, when the deceased Sivakantamma was traveling in Auto bearing registration No.KA-29/A-0612 from Korwar to Malagan village, at that time the driver of the auto drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, as a result of which, the auto overturned (turtled) causing grievous injuries to Sivakantamma and other occupants.
Later, the Sivakantamma succumbed to the injuries.
Husband and the children of the deceased filed claim petition claiming compensation.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:3703-DB HC-KAR 3.

The Tribunal while awarding compensation held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the auto driver and the deceased Sivakantamma succumbed to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled for compensation and accordingly awarded a sum of Rs.32,83,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till actual realization.

4. The primary contention of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant-Insurance Company is that the husband and the major son of the deceased Sivakantamma are not the dependents, as they themselves have stated in the claim petition that they are working as coolies.
Therefore, it is argued that presumption of dependency does not arise and the deduction towards personal expenses ought to have been 1/3rd instead of 1/4th as considered by the Tribunal.
It is further contended that there is no nexus between the accident and the subsequent death of deceased.

Reference NC:
2025:KHC-K:3703-DB HC-KAR is made to Ex.P8 and Ex.P9, stating that the deceased was discharged from the hospital in a stable condition, albeit against medical advice.
It is argued that due to the negligence on part of the claimants in not ensuring proper post discharge care, the deceased eventually succumbed to her injuries.

In light of the same, it is submitted that the death The Manager Shriram General Insurance ... vs Gundappa And Ors on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134000590/
3 cannot be directly, attributed to the accident and therefore, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to pay compensation.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the claimants relying upon the decision of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Birendar and Others1 (Birendar) submits that the compensation awarded constitutes part of the estate of the deceased and therefore, the legal representatives of the deceased are entitled to claim and receive compensation.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Birendar and Others1 (Birendar)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is contended that the Tribunal has rightly awarded (2020) 11 SCC 356 NC: 2025:KHC-K:3703-DB HC-KAR compensation and the same does not warrant any interference.
6. The Apex Court in the case of Birendar stated supra has held that the legal representatives of deceased have right to apply for compensation.

Further held that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The Apex Court affirming that the term "legal representative" in Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is broad and includes all legal heirs,
regardless of dependency.
Therefore, the Tribunal was right in holding that the husband and the major son being the legal representative are entitled for compensation, even if they are earning or not directly dependent.

The claimants are four in numbers and the NC: 2025:KHC-K:3703-DB HC-KAR deduction to be applied is 1/4th in light of the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2.
7.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insofar as the contention of the appellant that the death was not attributable to the accident occurred, it is argued that the deceased was discharged from the hospital in a stable condition, and that his eventual death was due to post discharge negligence.
However, it cannot be overlooked that unless conclusively established to the contrary, the later demise of the injured is presumed to have resulted from the injuries sustained in the accident.
Thus, the said contention is found to be devoid of merit, and the finding of the Tribunal that the death was a consequence of the accident is affirmed.
